title: Elizondo neither confirms nor denies being read into Immaculate Constellation
place_text: House Oversight Committee hearing, Washington, D.C.

tellings.quote: he was asked if he was read into Immaculate constellation he had a very interesting answer he said I can neither confirm nor deny
I would not be authorized to confirm nor deny the existence of any ongoing or past program
tellings.difference: Quotes his wording as not being authorized to confirm or deny any ongoing or past program, and brings in Shellenberger, Mace and Corbell.
tellings.link_reason: Both describe Elizondo at the 2024 congressional hearing neither confirming nor denying Immaculate Constellation.

as_told.title: Elizondo declines to confirm Immaculate Constellation at congressional hearing

plain: At a 2024 hearing of the House Oversight Committee in Washington, a man named Luis Elizondo was asked whether he had been briefed into Immaculate Constellation, a secret UFO program named in a report brought out by the journalist Michael Shellenberger, and he answered that he could neither confirm nor deny it. Michels points to that answer as telling, since a flat denial would have been easy if no such program existed. Elizondo himself later recalls his words a little differently on the show: that he would not be authorised to confirm or deny the existence of any ongoing or past program.
